=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .github/workflows/implement.yml:lines 2487-2498 | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_1-fast]
  PROBLEM: The `rm -rf .serena` cleanup lacks a tracked-tree guard after the project.yml hash check, so a repo-owned `.serena/**` tree can still be deleted.
  WHY: If `.serena/project.yml` matches the bootstrap hash but the repository tracks another `.serena` file, the cleanup still removes the directory and drops tracked content.
- scripts/implement_diagnose_post_codex_failure.sh:lines 98-152 | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_1-fast]
  PROBLEM: `patch_diagnose_reasoning_into_config` unconditionally assumes `tomllib`, which can fail on Python <3.11.
  WHY: Under a Python 3.10 runner, the diagnose script would abort before emitting post-Codex diagnosis.
- scripts/setup_serena.sh:lines 165-228 | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_1-fast]
  PROBLEM: `is_serena_header` regex `r"^\[mcp_servers\.serena(?:\.[^\]]+)?\](?:[ \t]+#.*)?$"` misses nested `[mcp_servers.serena.subtable] # comment`.
  WHY: Nested Serena tables would not be stripped, which can leave config bloat or duplicate registration.
- tests/test_implement_post_codex_recovery.py:lines 1123-1180 | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_1-fast]
  PROBLEM: The test asserts `state.get("created_issues", []) == []` but does not validate the `handled=false` output file.
  WHY: A regression in diagnose output shape could still pass because the test only checks that no issues were created.
- scripts/validate_process.sh:ensure_serena_bootstrap() ~line 650 (bootstrap_env_file mktemp)
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_1-fast]
  PROBLEM: `mktemp` in `${RUNTIME_DIR}` risks collision if parallel jobs run there.
  WHY: A safer unique-tempfile strategy would reduce the chance of interference between concurrent jobs.
- scripts/review_commit_changes.sh:~line 139 (git add -u pathspec)
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_1-fast]
  PROBLEM: `':!.serena/**'` excludes `.serena` changes but does not warn when repo-owned `.serena` content exists.
  WHY: Without an explicit warning, `.serena` changes can be silently ignored during commit cleanup.
